about.title: Brawley Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash on Rt 111, Rt 86, or one of Brawley's other busy corridors takes a loved one's life, the grief is immediate but the legal questions often arrive later. Imperial County families in this situation are usually navigating unfamiliar territory: who is allowed to bring a claim, what losses can be recovered, and how much time there is to act. California law limits who may file a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to other dependents in some cases. Brawley's traffic data shows collisions clustering on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., a pattern that reflects how ordinary commutes can turn tragic. We handle wrongful death claims and don't charge any upfront fee; we work on contingency, meaning we only recover if your family does.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California restricts wrongful death standing to specific family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and we can clarify where your family fits.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window, which matters given Brawley's mix of city, county, and state-maintained roads.

items.title: No Upfront Cost While Grieving
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made, so your family isn't asked to pay out of pocket during an already difficult time.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law prioritizes the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. We can review your family's specific circumstances to determine who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Brawley?
items.answer: Generally, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, such as a stretch maintained by Imperial County or Caltrans on Rt 86, the deadline to act can be much shorter, so it's worth discussing your timeline promptly.

items.question: What kinds of losses can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the deceased would have contributed, and the loss of companionship, guidance, and love the family experiences. Every situation is different, and we can walk through what may apply to your case.

items.question: Do you charge anything for your wrongful death services?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your family recovers compensation. There is no upfront fee.
